clue.text: Good-looking homes, and well-designed

indicators.note: well-designed suggests the letters are laid out afresh in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Houses that are attractive and thoughtfully built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well-designed' rearranges the letters of HOMES and AND.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an attractive, fine-featured person or thing is described this way.

clue.text: Harry has to have painters in

indicators.note: with 'in' later, to have something in says one piece is placed inside another
completes 'to have ... in', putting the painters inside the word has

parts.note: RAs are Royal Academicians, members of the Royal Academy of Arts, so painters

explanation.surface: A man called Harry must let decorators into his house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a man's name but is the verb meaning to pester; Royal Academicians are the conventional crossword painters.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry is to pester or torment persistently, the same as to badger someone.

clue.text: Panels representing an ancient city

indicators.note: representing hints the letters are re-presented in a different order

explanation.surface: Decorative panels depict a city from antiquity.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian port was founded by Greeks as Neapolis, so it is a city of antiquity.

clue.text: Went around dressed in woman's clothing

definitions.meaning: to go round the edge of something, avoiding it
wearing a skirt, read as a verb formed from the garment

explanation.surface: Someone avoided the issue while wearing a dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Avoiding a topic is going round its border; wearing the garment is being clad in it.

clue.text: Get together as appropriate

definitions.meaning: to assemble or gather with others
fitting or proper, an old adjectival sense

explanation.surface: People gather when it is fitting to do so.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is assembling; the other is an old word for fitting or suitable.

clue.text: Beats putting a portion back in the steamer!

indicators.note: in places the turned-round portion inside the steamer abbreviation

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

indicators.note: back means the word for a portion is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: a portion is a part

explanation.surface: An exclamation about returning a share of something aboard a steamship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns PART into TRAP, which goes 'in' SS.
explanation.definitionFit: To strap someone is to thrash them with a leather belt, so it means to hit repeatedly.

clue.text: Anger occasioned over a sort of art-work

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece over another comes first

parts.note: anger is temper

explanation.surface: Someone's rage was provoked about a painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasioned' is only a link here; in a down clue 'over' puts TEMPER above A.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a painting method using pigment bound in egg yolk, so a kind of artwork.

clue.text: Music and dance for taking off?

parts.note: an air is a tune, a piece of music
a strip, as in striptease, is a dance of undressing

explanation.surface: A show of music and dancing with an undressing theme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking off?' reads as undressing, the dance theme, but points to aircraft leaving the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A runway area from which aircraft take off into the sky.

clue.text: 25 has time for the very lowest class

parts.note: 25-down is the beast that charges; a steer is a young castrated one
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A clue referring to another answer saying it has a period for the humblest group.
explanation.definitionFit: On ships the cheapest passenger accommodation was below decks near the rudder gear.

clue.text: Went and married again?

definitions.meaning: betook oneself, as in going to a place
paired once more, read as re- plus the verb for coupling

explanation.surface: Someone left and got wed a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is an old verb for going; split after re- it means coupled once more.

clue.text: Fine for being caught in a pool

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation for caught is placed within the word for a pool

parts.note: a mere is a lake or pond
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A penalty for being found in a swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' looks like an adjective or noun; it is the verb to penalise.
explanation.definitionFit: An old legal verb meaning to punish someone with a monetary penalty.

clue.text: Many in distress get awfully tight-fisted

indicators.note: in places the letter for many inside the word for distress

parts.note: misery is distress
L is the Roman numeral fifty, used for many

explanation.surface: Many people who are suffering become stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being very mean with money, like a hoarder of cash.

clue.text: Has the proper cover

indicators.note: proper suggests the letters must be put into their right order

explanation.surface: Someone owns the correct covering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'proper' rearranges the letters of HAS and THE.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-fitting case, as for a blade or sword, is a protective covering.

clue.text: A firm ruler

parts.note: reads as a strict leader but means a board member who governs a company

explanation.surface: A strict leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A board member directs the running of a company, so rules a business.

clue.text: Raced around the outer edge and skidded

indicators.note: around says the word for raced encloses the word for an edge

parts.note: sped means raced
a lip is a rim or outer edge

explanation.surface: A driver went round the circuit's margin and lost grip.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing one's footing or grip and sliding is a skid.

clue.text: Mature Oriental sailor mixing with foreign element

parts.note: adult means mature
E stands for east, oriental
a rating is a non-commissioned sailor

explanation.surface: A grown-up Eastern seaman mixes with outsiders.
explanation.definitionFit: Debasing something by adding an impurity is contaminating it.

clue.text: Putting a good man among youngsters can cause strikes

indicators.note: among puts the good-man pieces inside the youngsters

parts.note: lambs are young sheep, youngsters
ST, saint, is a good man

explanation.surface: Placing a virtuous man among young people may lead to industrial action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strikes' is the verb meaning hits, not walkouts.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrash or berate someone is to hit them hard.

clue.text: Make a song about almost incredible prevaricating

indicators.note: about says the singing word goes round the other piece

parts.note: to sing is to make a song
a tall story is close to unbelievable

explanation.surface: Someone sings about something nearly unbelievable while evading.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing for time and avoiding a straight answer is evasion.

clue.text: The study of man embracing woman

definitions.text: The study of man embracing woman

parts.words: The study of man embracing woman
parts.note: reads as romance but describes the human sciences, which take in both sexes

explanation.surface: A man studies while hugging a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The science of humankind and its cultures covers men and women alike.

clue.text: To feel strongly about a lie's unusual

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters are arranged in an uncommon way

parts.note: the word lie's taken as lies, its letters spelt out

explanation.surface: Someone is upset that a falsehood is out of the ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges A and LIES into ALISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp something fully and vividly is to become aware of it.

clue.text: A Greek maid leaves after the festivity

indicators.note: after puts the leaves piece following the festivity

parts.note: a gala is a festive occasion
tea is leaves for brewing

explanation.surface: A young woman from Greece departs once the party ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb but is the noun, tea leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth she was the sea nymph, and the statue brought to life by Pygmalion.

clue.text: The country offers a fellow a quiet retirement

indicators.note: retirement means going backwards, so the whole run is reversed

parts.note: a man is a fellow
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet

explanation.surface: A nation provides a man with a peaceful time after work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' turns A MAN A P backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A Central American state, known for its canal.

clue.text: Still treats constituents badly

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters are messed up into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone continues to treat their staff poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: Being motionless and in repose means not moving.

clue.text: The 25 one's giving for some fruit

parts.note: 25-down is the beast, given as its own word
an ace is one, so one's gives aces

explanation.surface: A reference to another answer yielding produce.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild plums related to the damson are a small orchard fruit.

clue.text: Gasp for breath when about 51-not stiff though

indicators.note: when about says the panting word goes round the number

parts.note: to pant is to gasp for breath
LI is fifty-one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Breathless around a number but flexible.
explanation.definitionFit: Flexible and easily bent, the opposite of rigid.

clue.text: The beast might charge one-and there's a ludicrous statement!

definitions.meaning: a male bovine that may rush at you

explanation.surface: An animal may rush at you, and that is a silly thing to say.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the male animal; the other is a comically illogical remark.

clue.text: The odd trip is taken to show enterprise

indicators.note: odd suggests the letters are made strange by reordering them

explanation.surface: A strange journey shows adventurousness.
explanation.definitionFit: Courage and drive are synonyms for get-up-and-go.

clue.text: For the traveller's pack of cards?

definitions.text: For the traveller's pack of cards?

parts.words: For the traveller's pack of cards?
parts.note: reads as playing cards but means a case for suits of clothes

explanation.surface: A deck of cards for the traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: Luggage for holding clothes, punning on hearts, clubs and the rest.

clue.text: Bringing back a number of soldiers could make an impression

indicators.note: bringing back means the whole run is read in reverse

parts.note: ten is a number
GIs are US soldiers

explanation.surface: Withdrawing troops might leave a mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bringing back' reverses the whole run; the definition describes what the object does rather than naming it, which is fair for a seal ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring with a seal is pressed into wax to leave a mark.

clue.text: Acceptable excuses given by a worker

parts.note: pleas are excuses
an ant is a worker insect

explanation.surface: A labourer gives reasonable justifications.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreeable and nice, a synonym for satisfactory.
